questions.question: What does the 'S' in HTTPS stand for?
questions.answer: Secure

questions.question: What icon typically indicates a secure HTTPS connection?
questions.answer: Lock

questions.question: If a site only uses HTTP, what should you avoid doing?
questions.answer: Submitting passwords

questions.question: How does HTTPS protect user data?
questions.answer: It encrypts communication

questions.question: Which of the following indicates a potentially less secure site?
questions.answer: http://login.com

questions.question: What setting can help ensure secure browsing by default?
questions.answer: Force HTTPS connections

questions.question: Why should browsers be updated regularly?
questions.answer: To receive security patches

questions.question: What risk comes with granting microphone access to websites?
questions.answer: Unauthorized audio recording

questions.question: Which browser permission can leak your location?
questions.answer: Location

questions.question: What should users consider before granting browser permissions?
choices: How their data will be used
questions.answer: How their data will be used

questions.question: Which of the following passwords is considered weak and commonly used?
questions.answer: all of the above

questions.question: Why is using pet names as passwords risky?
questions.answer: They are predictable

questions.question: Which of these is the most secure password?
questions.answer: a7d1G9#pQ!

questions.question: What makes using common passwords like 'qwerty' a bad practice?
choices: They are easy for hackers to guess through dictionary attacks
questions.answer: They are easy for hackers to guess through dictionary attacks

questions.question: What is one of the main reasons why people continue using easily guessable passwords, despite security risks?
choices: They are often simple to remember
questions.answer: They are often simple to remember

questions.question: What is the recommended minimum length for a secure password?
questions.answer: 16 characters

questions.question: Which of these methods will strengthen your password?
choices: Using your name as a password
Using a memorable phrase with random characters
Using the same password for multiple accounts
questions.answer: Using a memorable phrase with random characters

questions.question: Why is it important to use a different password for each account?
choices: To make it easier to remember passwords
To avoid compromising multiple accounts if one password is breached
To allow all accounts to be easily accessed by one password manager
questions.answer: To avoid compromising multiple accounts if one password is breached

questions.question: What is a passphrase and why is it considered stronger than a regular password?
choices: A passphrase is a random collection of letters that are hard to remember
A passphrase is a long phrase made up of random words or characters that is difficult to guess
A passphrase is a short, common word
questions.answer: A passphrase is a long phrase made up of random words or characters that is difficult to guess

questions.question: What is the advantage of using a password manager?
choices: It helps generate and store secure, unique passwords for each account
It simplifies password recovery for forgotten passwords
It stores passwords in an unencrypted format
It avoids the need for multi-factor authentication
questions.answer: It helps generate and store secure, unique passwords for each account

questions.question: What is multi-factor authentication (MFA)?
choices: A method to verify your identity using a password only
A process that uses only biometrics for authentication
A method that adds an extra layer of security by requiring more than just a password
A method that automatically logs you in without needing authentication
questions.answer: A method that adds an extra layer of security by requiring more than just a password

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of multi-factor authentication?
choices: Logging in with just your password
Entering a password and receiving a one-time passcode on your phone
Using the same password across multiple sites
Using only a username and email address
questions.answer: Entering a password and receiving a one-time passcode on your phone

questions.question: Which of the following methods is commonly used in multi-factor authentication?
choices: Biometric data (e.g., fingerprint or facial recognition)
questions.answer: Biometric data (e.g., fingerprint or facial recognition)

questions.question: Why should you enable multi-factor authentication on your online accounts?
choices: To improve the overall security of your accounts by adding another verification step
Because it reduces the need to remember passwords
questions.answer: To improve the overall security of your accounts by adding another verification step

questions.question: What is the purpose of using an authenticator app for multi-factor authentication?
choices: It generates a unique code every few seconds for login verification
It automatically logs you into all websites
questions.answer: It generates a unique code every few seconds for login verification

questions.question: Which action helps prevent phishing attacks?

questions.question: What should you do if a message pressures you to act immediately?
choices: Click the link before it expires

questions.question: What is the first step when a cybersecurity incident is detected?
